meta.notes: The living woman, met on visited dates before 19 July 1929. She is good company and a sharp edit, and sometimes wrong about who a picture belongs to. She has no idea who is holding her corner. No foreshadowing: she is having a good year. Her name and gender are ordinary knowledge, never a reveal. At the Harukiya she is enjoying herself and wants more of it. No song, card or line of hers refers forward.

threads.source: Her weekly loss. S03's plate joke is Nadia's scene, not this one.

threads.topic: That's a cheap magazine for a serious shop.
threads.source: World. Aliens are common and ignore people. Atmosphere only; no message, no faction.

threads.topic: Miss Sato's picture isn't in the window any more.
threads.source: WR-07. She is wrong here and half knows it. S06 is its scene.
JF008-A01. First talk about working with anyone. Nobody in the house is implied.
JF012-A01. Owner put it back on the table. The target is the customer's hypocrisy and never the men she means. Needs a history check on the Pleasure Man talk of that winter.
B02. The loan she will not recognise. No wink at it; only the player knows.
B08 to B10 and the O2 branches. Each flag writes one line in the key book. Never shows her going up after agreeing not to.

Owner ruling 2026-10-31: she did it. Told plainly and early by her, so it is never a reveal. Only people with power; nobody at either address. Plates brought to her for developing, so she is never the bait.

threads.source: Holmes Airport opened Saturday 16 March 1929. She has a plate and a Saturday. Has no door yet; read through the playtest panel.

av_w1s.line: You can stand there, night man, but you're in my light and I'm charging you for it.

av_w2.line: No, higher on the glass. I'm not trying to improve the street. Mrs. Owen, going to Congress. The Speaker wants to know where she'll hang her hat.

av_w3b.line: I buy it every day. A woman has to have a vice she can leave in a window.

choices.label: Why the roof? You keep looking up there.

av_w4.line: You've got the keys to the only decent horizon in Long Island City and you use it to look at pipes. If you ever want a sky taken properly, I'd take it for the price of the door.

av_d1.line: I have been expelled from twenty-four literary societies. One of them was founded expressly to hear my appeal. The Derby is the only body that keeps writing back. Here's Saturday's. Why did the portrait sue? It had been framed.

av_d1s.line: Silence. He sends that too, but on better paper.

av_d2.line: Thank you. Terrible is a category. He only files the merely bad ones. Last week he sent mine back marked "told to us by our father."

av_d3.line: He will not. Don't be kind, night man, it's bad for the form.

av_s1.line: Fifteen cents. "The visitor from the fourth dimension could explain the universe. I tied my shoelace and he asked me to do it again." I keep it for the pictures. They've drawn him with a collar.

choices.label: Have you ever got one of the real ones on a plate?

av_s2.line: Six. A smear, a smear, a very fine smear of the gasworks. They went over again Tuesday and didn't look down. I've had sitters like that. Aldermen, mostly.

av_s3.line: I believe it's fifteen cents. The ones over the river are real enough. I just wouldn't take their word on a shoelace.

av_r1.line: Noticed that, did you? Best thing I've done since Christmas. Her whole face stops performing for a fiftieth of a second. She wants it burned.

av_r1s.line: Go on. Everyone else has an opinion and you've got a wrench, so I expect yours is better.

av_r2.line: It's her face, and my fiftieth of a second, and I took it down, and I will keep that negative until one of us is dead. There. That's the most reasonable I get.

av_r3.line: Thank you, that's what I've been telling myself. You'd think it would sound better from a stranger.

av_h1.line: I asked for somebody to help hang my pictures. One proposed marriage, one proposed a duel, and the third actually brought a hammer. I hired the third. He's crooked on the left. I've kept it, it annoys the right sort of person.

av_m1.line: She'd come for her plates and stayed for the Pleasure Man crowd. "One cannot trust a man who admires another man." I said you say that, madam, and you have married three of them. She'll be back. She's got two more husbands to have copied.

av_k1.line: Tonight? You're a prince of the service stair. Give me that and put me in your book. I'll be up there till the sky stops being interesting, and I'll sign for it like a citizen.

av_k2.line: Your capitals are terrible. Look, hold it like a grease pencil, from up here. You'd be surprised how much of a person's character is in the E.

choices.label: You know that's a lightning rod you'll be standing by.

av_k3.line: I do not enter the lion's den on the assumption of divine protection. I have a bill for the lion.

av_n1.line: Night man. Your clock and my watch have just agreed about something, which makes one of us. You're carrying the book. Storm's coming over the Gate and I'd like my door.

choices.label: Don't go up. Stay in the shop.
Let me come up with you.
Bring Miss Quell and Mr. Ewald tonight. Not Monday.

av_n1s.line: You look like somebody reading their own handwriting. The key, if it's all the same.

av_n2.line: Good. Nineteenth, A.V., roof, storm. Spell it how you like, the E's your own problem now.

av_n3.line: All right. It's your roof. I don't know what I've done to it, but I'm sure there's a form.

av_n4.line: Is that the maintenance department's view of the weather? No, don't. You've gone a very bad colour. Fine. I've got prints to wash. Nobody ever died of an evening with a clean enlarger.

av_n4b.line: Don't thank me, you'll give me the idea I've done something. Go on. Mind your pipes.

av_n5.line: Can you hold a focusing cloth in a gale and not talk? Then you're better staffed than the Record.

av_n6.line: Half past six? For a schedule to a deed? You've read it, haven't you. Nobody reads it. All right, night man, go and get them, and if they bring Mrs. Kessler I'm charging her for the chair.

av_b1.line: Two aldermen, a landlord and a man from the Board of Estimate. People bring me plates to develop and forget I can read. I keep a print, and they know I keep it.

av_b2.line: I don't sell anything. I keep it where the sitter can think about it. Jackson Avenue got its lamps in an afternoon, and I have never once had to say a number.

av_b3.line: It is. So was what he did with the lamp money. Jackson Avenue got its lamps in an afternoon, and I sleep very well.

av_b4.line: Nobody across the road, mind, and nobody in this arcade. You don't squeeze people you borrow sugar from.

av_p1.line: You're between my drummer and the door, night man, and she's been looking for a reason. Stay if you're staying. We open on money, then I get up, then we try something quiet and find out whose fault it is.

av_p2.line: Second number, about the middle. I stand, the piano stops, which surprises nobody but the piano, and Lily holds up the whole room on a snare for as long as I can get away with. By the finish I've hung a hat on her cymbal stand. The Speaker wanted to know where Mrs. Owen would hang hers.

av_p4.line: Mine. The slow one wants something in the last eight bars and I keep bringing it the wrong thing. Lily goes back to the bass for that one so she can stand further away from me.

av_l1.line: Read this. No, I'll read it, you'd do it no justice. "The Ravenswood Sound Shorts Company of Astoria has had favourable report of your act, and proposes to test same on the premises." I sent them a photograph in February and they sent a man to drink here and see if it was true. He didn't leave during the slow one. I told Lily on the eighteenth. Lily said ask what happens to the recording, so I asked. This is the answer.

av_l2.line: It's very good news. I've wanted somebody with a letterhead to say that since before you had that coat. It's also four pages, and I've been through them.

av_l3.line: Clause two, their arrangement, fixed as tested. Clause four, the concern selects the still. Clause six. It's sound on film, night man. They put my voice through a slit of light, some boy in Astoria develops it in the same soup I buy by the gallon, and clause six says the concern retains the negative.

av_l4.line: When it has my name, my picture and my take, I'll sign it on the bar. It's gone back in grease pencil. I do want this, you understand. I've got the routes page out of Variety folded in the music: the Original Georgia Five, Danceland, Jamaica. That's a train, not the moon. I'd like to be a train away from somebody's good opinion.

choices.label: You know people who could lean on them.

av_l5.line: They've answered. Clause nine: the premises to hold a licence under the Act. The Harukiya holds a wink.

av_l6.line: There's a man on the Board of Estimate who'd have them begging by Thursday. No. I'd like to find out what it's worth with nobody's arm behind its back. Don't look like that. I'm allowed one thing I've only got honestly.

av_q1.line: That's different. I took Miss Sato out of the window. Nobody's offering to take me out of every picture house between here and Jamaica.

av_q2.line: I know what I kept. You've got a very unpleasant way of holding a wrench.

av_q3.line: Why are you looking at me like that? You've got a very unpleasant way of holding a wrench.

av_t1.line: Four minutes and eleven seconds. Lily on the bass, and the last eight went where I've been trying to put them all year. The whole room came in early, clean over my two bars, and I had nothing to do but go with them. Juno had that thing going in her coat. I've heard it. It's the best we have ever been.

av_t2.line: That's what I said. Made by friends, no fixed arrangement, no clause six. Lily said it louder. There's one difficulty.

av_t3.line: You can hear Miss Sato. She came in on the last chorus and on the top note her voice went, clean in half, and she kept going, and it's the truest thing anybody's done on that stage since I've had the bench. She's under the whole of the last eight, Juno can't splice her out without splicing us. She wants it wiped.

av_t4.line: I know whose voice it is. I've had this conversation. I know how it goes. Go away, night man, I'm thinking.

av_t5.line: Thank you. I tried that on her. It worked no better in April.

av_c1.line: Cut. I went up to 2C and stood on Juno's rug while she did it, so I could say I'd seen it, and I carried it down to the ashcan like a bailiff. The best four minutes I ever got, in a coil, on top of somebody's eggshells.

av_c2.line: She asked me twice and she was right twice. Don't make a window card of it.

av_c3.line: No. That's as far as I go this month.

av_f1.line: That's the fifth. Look at the fourth first. Light from the left, you could read by it, and it's wrong, it's a wonderful picture of a woman who'd never get up from a bench. A photograph can advertise the wrong act. This one's right. This one, they can't select around.

av_f3.line: You're right there, that's your elbow.

av_f4.speaker: LILY
av_f4.line: It's a fine elbow. You said together, in March. Four pages you've sent them about who gets to choose the picture.

av_f5.line: (She looks at the print for longer than it needs.) I framed you out. I did that and didn't see it. I'm sorry. Pick the one you want.

av_f6.speaker: LILY
av_f6.line: I'm picking the ugly one. You're laughing in it and I've got both arms.

choices.label: Before the last eight. The two you added. Your hands have nothing to do.

av_v2.line: You do radiators. (She looks at the keys, then plays it through without them, straight in. Across the room the bass player, who had gone for her coat, puts the coat down.)

av_v3.speaker: LILY
av_v3.line: I told you that in March.

av_v4.line: You told me you liked it the old way. He told me which bar.

av_v5.speaker: LILY
av_v5.line: So when the man with the wrench says it, it's a discovery.

av_u1.line: Was it? Yes. It went where it goes. Is the kitchen shut? I want something with rice in it and I don't want to hear about the bridge.

av_u2.line: Yes. Don't make me useful for a minute. Tell me something about pipes. I mean it. Something nobody could sing.

choices.label: The third-floor riser knocks after the valve shuts.

av_o1.line: (Harukiya, before opening. Lily is working through the last eight bars on the bass when Adela comes in. Adela waits by the piano until she finishes, which takes some effort.) What?
av_o1.speaker: LILY

av_o4.line: Yes. Lovely. (She puts an envelope on the closed keyboard cover.)

av_o8.line: (She takes off her coat. One arm catches in the sleeve; she pulls too hard, gives up, and works the cuff loose.) The little picture concern in Astoria. The one I sent the photograph to.

av_o9.line: The photograph you said was only an inquiry.
av_o9.speaker: LILY

av_o10.line: It was. They've inquired back. (She has read the letter often enough to go straight to the paragraph.) They want to hear the act. Here. A recording test, if the room is suitable. Two numbers.

av_o12.line: (She nods. For a moment her smile loses its practised shape.) They asked when we could be ready.

av_o13.line: (She reaches for the letter. Adela gives it to her, then tries to read over her shoulder.) I can read it from this side.
av_o13.speaker: LILY

av_o14.line: I know. There's a bit near the bottom.

av_o15.line: I'm getting there. (Adela puts her hands in her coat pockets, finds she is still holding the coat, and puts it down.) They liked the photograph.
av_o15.speaker: LILY

av_o17.line: You sent the one where you look as though you've just dismissed the orchestra.
av_o17.speaker: LILY

av_o18.line: It's a useful expression. Saves postage later. (Lily laughs. Adela sits and opens the piano.) Listen. I thought, for the second number. (She plays the lead-in to the last eight, then changes it: the bass figure gives way to a rising chord, held where the next phrase should begin. She sings the phrase without words, adds another small ascent, and brings it home.) There.

av_o19.line: (She is looking at the music.) Where do I come in?
av_o19.speaker: LILY

av_o22.line: (She plays it again, pointing with her chin as her hands land.) There. Two bars later.

av_o25.line: And taken out the pulse underneath you.
av_o25.speaker: LILY

av_o26.line: I want some space for the line.

av_o27.line: Then keep the space we rehearsed. You can take your time over the bass.
av_o27.speaker: LILY

av_o29.line: Is that what it sounded like last night?
av_o29.speaker: LILY

av_o31.line: We spent an hour finding those bars.
av_o31.speaker: LILY

av_o32.line: I know. I've had another thought.

av_o34.line: (She starts the new passage again. Lily doesn't join her. After a few notes she stops.) You haven't tried it.

av_o35.line: I don't want my part to be waiting for you to decide you've finished.
av_o35.speaker: LILY

av_o37.line: Perhaps. I like what I play there. You liked it yesterday.
av_o37.speaker: LILY

av_o38.line: (She looks down at her hands.) I still like it.

av_o39.line: Well, it isn't in this one.
av_o39.speaker: LILY

av_o40.line: (A chair scrapes in the bar. She waits for it to stop.) They'll only hear us once. At first, I mean. They won't know which night it usually comes right.

av_o41.line: So let's play the version we know.
av_o41.speaker: LILY

av_o42.line: I think this could be better.

av_o43.line: It could. We could spend the whole week on it and find out. Have you told them yes?
av_o43.speaker: LILY

av_o44.line: I said we could arrange an evening.

av_o45.line: (Her hand falls from the strings.) Before asking me.
av_o45.speaker: LILY

av_o46.line: I didn't give them a date.

av_o48.line: (She draws breath. Lily waits, without helping her out of it.) Yes. I did. I'm sorry. (She closes the music over the new bars.) Would you like to do the test?

av_o49.line: (She picks up the letter and reads the last paragraph properly.) I want to know what happens to the recording afterward.
av_o49.speaker: LILY

av_o50.line: So do I. And whether they pay for a test.

av_o51.line: Ask both before arranging our evening.
av_o51.speaker: LILY

av_o53.line: (She hands the letter back.) Yes. I'd like to do it.
av_o53.speaker: LILY

av_o54.line: (She presses her lips together. It doesn't quite contain the smile.)

av_o55.line: You could have started with that question.
av_o55.speaker: LILY

av_o56.line: I had a very composed entrance prepared.

av_o58.line: (She laughs, then looks at the closed music.) I do still want to try the two bars.

av_o60.line: After we've played the old one?

av_o61.line: Once through as it stands. Then show me the new part slowly. I want to see if there's something I can play under it. And we choose together. You don't send them another improved version tonight.
av_o61.speaker: LILY

av_o62.line: (She reaches for her pencil, hesitates, and puts it on the piano between them.) Together.

av_o63.line: (She settles her hand on the bass. Adela opens the old arrangement, checks the first chord, and looks up for the count. They get through the verse. At the last eight the familiar figure comes in beneath her voice, and she lets it carry the phrase farther than she did last night. When the sound has gone, neither speaks immediately.)
av_o63.speaker: LILY

av_o66.line: (She turns back one page.) Now let me show you what I meant.

av_e4.speaker: LILY
av_e4.line: You changed it. For Astoria. Are we showing them the act, or the next one?

av_e5.line: All right, let me show you. (She reaches across for the chart, stops, and holds out her hand for it instead.) May I?

choices.label: What you want there is a little more feeling.

av_a1.line: Everyone's come to look at the sky. It's the only time you get a whole crowd with its mouth open and nobody posing. I've got one plate, so I'm being very rude about who stands in front of me.

choices.label: You could be home by dark.

av_a2.line: I could be, and I'd have a window full of plucky girls who flew somewhere. I'd like one who's only standing by a wing and thinking about her lunch. Hold my bag.

av_l4s.line: Go on, then. You've got a radiator somewhere.
